posts.author: Lahrs
posts.body: I've been wanting to create a game similar to Knights of Pen and Paper, a game within a game. Before I purchase the RPG Maker software, is this something that can be done or should I keep looking for a different game creation software? Not that I necessarily know what I'm doing programming wise, but I am familiar with the much older versions of RPGMaker.

That should have been an obvious thing to do on my part that I clearly whiffed at. Thank you for bringing that to my attention so I can fix it.
I'm going to steal part of their tagline as it explains it better than I can.
"Take on the roles of in-game players taking on the roles of their characters in a traditional pen and paper RPG session in the ultimate meta roleplaying experience.
Choose from multiple classes, such as knights and mages, pick your characters to control those classes, like grandma or kid brother, and take on the loads of quests, monsters, items and equipment littered throughout. Blacksmiths, enchanters, mining, gathering, hidden treasures and a whole lot more await, giving players a lot of room to personalize their gameplay experience."
Knights of Pen and Paper Steam page.
Currently three players (up to 5) face the GM. The GM is reading the story, and the fight happens behind him. Here you can see the bats that the players will attack.
Another fight scene
Choosing skills during battle
Sample character sheet
You choose a character: student, cool guy, geek, etc. each with their own bonus. Then each character chooses a class: cleric, fighter, wizard, etc. that has their own skills and stat increases. Those are the players that sit at the table. So you can end up with Cool Guy Cleric, or Student Cleric, or Geek Fighter, etc.
The story unfolds from the DM's perspective, with the dialogue, NPC's and fights all transpiring behind the DM as if the story was being visualized behind him. Rather than normal travel on a world map, the location would be static with the players around the table. The story, with occasional NPCs and the battles all happen above the DM. Travel is on an overland map, where the players can move between locations with a roll of the die. Passing means safe travels, a failure results in a fight.
The first game was great, second built on it, but after the second game was released it turned into a horrible P2W game, and 3 is universally loathed. I would like to take a stab at the style of game without needing microtransactions or anything. I have no grand plans of selling it or anything, but just to make something fun and different.
Knights of Pen and Paper 3
Here is the link to the newest game in the series. Has some updated ideas, but was abandoned by the developers to keep the P2W money rolling in on the mobile version. At the very least you can see the preview video that might help show more of what I am looking to do.

posts.author: cchmaster
posts.body:
I've played this game. I'll say, yes. It can be done, but not easy. RM is designed for regular JRPG(not a precise term, but you know what I mean), so it can help you to store most of the game database, including characters, monsters, states, stats, equipment, and so on, but you need to do all the others, including the UI, game menu, and game flow. To achieve those, you'll need plugins, which means money, or you can do it all by yourself, which means spending time to learn.
I don't know about other engines, but you can check what they can give you and what else you need.

posts.author: Mac15001900
posts.body:
Depends on both how close do you need your game to be to that and how much effort are you willing to put into it. That battle scene can probably be achieved just by adding the table graphic onto a regular front-view battle, as long as you're fine with the UI being RPG Maker's default. If you want that table to be in some way dynamic, you'd need to implement that behaviour yourself, the engine wouldn't really help.
Note that from you post I'm assuming you're fine with learning some JavaScript to achieve this - it would be rather difficult without that, unless you're fine with paying someone to do it.

posts.author: AquaEcho
posts.body: Yes it's doable with a lot of plugins. However, there are issues with using VisuStella besides the cost. A bigger problem is that they pack a ton of features in each plugin, resulting in overwriting engine code you might not want it to and creating conflicts with other plugins. On top of that the code is obfuscated, affecting performance and making it so other plugin devs can't make compatibility patches. So you end up having to choose between a VisuStella plugin you paid for and another plugin you want.

posts.author: ZombieKidzRule
posts.body:
So, it has been quite a while since I played the game, but I am pretty sure that I have learned enough to Event the vast majority of this type of game with only a couple of free, default plugins that come with MZ. Namely the ButtonPicture and TextPicture plugins.
And I have a couple of simple plugins that were created with help from people here on the forum that would also be free. One allows you to show more than 100 pictures at a time on the screen. If you ended up needing those, I could help out with that.
The hardest part for me would be recreating the Character Sheet UI and, of course, the graphics.
Now, if you aren't set on the game looking really similar, then there are lots of options for the graphics that are free. There are a ton of Icons that could be used as well as a lot of free assets here on the forum and on sites like Pixabay.
Again, based on my experience, I think the hardest part would be creating a similar Character Sheet UI and that is only because I haven't explored plugins for that and Eventing it would be complex, but I don't think impossible.
The other challenge would be programming the enemy part of combat. Meaning who the enemy chooses to target. Because I wouldn't use the default MZ combat system. I would Event my own.
Anyway, it might be easier to recreate with a bunch of plugins for someone who is more experienced with using plugins. But I just wanted to mention that I think this entire game could pretty much be replicated with just a handful of plugins that are free. But it would be quite a bit of work and it would require you to invest a lot of time in really learning MZ and some Java Script.
Just my opinion though based on what I have learned so far. I might be entirely wrong. But if you are really interested, there is much to be gained by trying.
And I have learned a lot by trying to recreate what I like in other games.
Good luck with whatever you decide to do and feel free to reach out if you think there is anything I can assist with.

Click to expand...
By using a number of plugins you can create the feel of your original game and transfer about half of it's ruleset.  If you want to replicate it faithfully, it will require you to learn simple java and write your own plugins or hire someone else to do so for you.  Way I see it you have these options:
Obtain the plugins you need for free or cheap.  Use RPGmaker to approximate your game.  Release it and call it a day.
Do the above, but hire programmers to create all the custom plugins you will need to do precisely what you need.
Find a different platform.  I do not believe a platform exists that can do what you are asking without coding knowledge.
My suggestion is to use RPGmaker MV.  If you have the patience and dedication to see this thing through it can be done well.  Consider making a Knights of Pen and Paper inspired game, a similar but improved version of the original.  RPG maker would be awesome at the latter.

posts.author: ZimXero

posts.author: Mac15001900
posts.body:
Lahrs said:
why MV over MZ?
Click to expand...
I think generally the greater amount of plugins might make it easier to customise things, which sounds like it'd be useful in this project. MZ doesn't really have an equivalent of Graphic Design Mode for example, or anything similar that would allow for UI customisation.
It's definitely possible to do it in either, and I'd recommend looking up some MV vs MZ comparisons out there before deciding. MZ does have some neat QoL improvements and nicer mapping, but MV should make the technical part easier thanks to its plugins.

posts.author: AquaEcho
posts.body:
Basically MV is cheaper and has a bigger plugin library. What this means is you usually have half a dozen options for any one feature you want to add. Yanfly suite is a lot cheaper than VisuStella (Yanfly ported to MZ) and the code isn't obfuscated so you can get patches to fix incompatibilities with other plugins. Even then, you can get away with using no Yanfly at all just because there are so many alternatives.
MZ has more editor features, namely the map editor is nicer, but a lot fewer plugins. A lot of people use VisuStella just because it's convenient but it has the problems I described earlier. Also to note if you have both MV and MZ you can just use MZ as a map editor for an MV project.
